claims.text: Nanolayered CoCrFeNi/graphene composites can be fabricated.
The graphene interlayer can be a monolayer or otherwise ultrathin.
The metal/graphene interfaces in the proposed coating are coherent and well controlled.
Coherent graphene interlayers increase resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation relative to homogeneous or incoherent-interface controls.
Metal/graphene interfaces affect dislocation-mediated deformation in nanolayered CoCrFeNi/graphene composites.
Coherent metal/graphene interfaces block or pin dislocations.
Interruption of dislocation glide and dynamic recovery slows creep.
Dislocations encountering coherent interlayers pile up or bypass the interfaces.
Dislocation pile-up or bypass significantly raises the local stress required for continued plastic flow.
Disruption of dislocation propagation increases the activation energy for creep deformation.
Disruption of dislocation propagation lowers the steady-state creep strain rate.
Coatings with coherent interlayers will have lower creep strain rates than homogeneous coatings or multilayers with incoherent interfaces.
Coatings with coherent interlayers will have higher measured activation energies for plastic deformation than the controls.
Coatings with coherent interlayers will exhibit a delayed onset of inelastic deformation.
At room to moderately elevated temperatures, dislocation motion is active while diffusion remains limited.
The proposed mechanism applies primarily when dislocation motion dominates plastic deformation.
Maintaining the interlayer thickness at a few nanometers preserves interface coherence.
Identical creep tests on coherent-interface and homogeneous or disrupted-interface controls provide a controlled comparison of the proposed mechanism.
Failure to observe lower creep rates, higher activation energies, and interface blocking of dislocations would falsify the proposed mechanism.
